//: The 23 round-trips of README 'Spawn an actor at a CHOSEN COORDINATE', as ONE request.
//needs: a tactical mission that is PLAYING; the plan's first step waits for HasAnyTurnStarted
//defName: must be specific enough that it is the FIRST find hit - find is a substring match

steps.//: The mission is driveable only once a turn has started. Level.CurrentState == Playing flips EARLIER (Level.cs:225) and waiting on it lands mid-setup.
The actor definition, out of the live def repository. defs[0] is a hard reference: no hit means a failed step, never a silent null.

steps.//PRELOAD: MANDATORY. `spawn` runs its ENTIRE spawn inside the asset-loading callback (TacticalDeployZone.cs:424 -> the callback at :409-423). Skip it and a def whose addressable assets are cold spawns a live, in-play, correctly-positioned actor with NO MODEL. Assets are per-DEF: this looked unnecessary once only because that run's def was already deployed on that map.

steps.//: LoadRoots (AssetsReferencesLoader.cs:71) not StartLoadingRoots (:58) - same acquisition (it calls StartLoadingRoots itself, so the level's Dispose at TacticalLevelController.cs:416 still releases it) but an iterator that ends when loading does. The game's own idiom: TacticalLevelController.cs:557-569.

Timing.Start (Timing.cs:246) returns the IUpdateable whose Stopped is a POSITIVE single-call predicate. The engine has no `not`, and both IsLoading surfaces are the wrong polarity and loader-global. The trailing null is the optional catchException - arity is matched exactly.
ASYNCHRONOUS - firing the load and spawning on the next round-trip waits for nothing.
def -> (ComponentSetDef, ActorInstanceData), exactly as the `spawn` console command does it (TacticalDeployZone.cs:412-413, ActorDeployData.cs:78,93).
Everything about the unit - EquipmentItems / Stats / BaseWill / AbilityTraits - is a settable field on this object. Add `call` set steps here for a loadout.
Whose side it is on. "" would mean the faction currently on turn.
Projects as {"$enum":"Intruder","type":"..."} and binds straight back as that same envelope - the round trip needs no hardcoded participant kind.
LayerMask's only field is private, so it comes back as a handle, not inline.
Snap the requested point onto a floor. Probe from ABOVE it: SnapXYZ casts down onto the mask.
ComponentSetDef.GetComponentDef<T> (ComponentSetDef.cs:19) picks the two defs CanStandAt needs - no paging through Components and no matching by name.

An ASSERTION written as a one-shot wait: CanStandAt returning false is ok:true with value false, so a plain `call` would sail past an unstandable point and spawn into a wall. A wait with timeoutMs 1 turns the predicate into a stop.
THE SPAWN, at the coordinate (TacticalDeployZone.cs:257). The 7-arg overload resolves with no sig.

The housekeeping `spawn` does after its own spawn (TacticalDeployZone.cs:415-422). Source = the actor itself is not a typo (:415). StartTurn is deliberately NOT called: the command only does it when the new actor's faction is the level's CurrentFaction.

COSMETIC TAIL, onError:continue on purpose. This re-runs selection, which asks the navmesh for a path; while the map rebuilds (in-combat explosions) it throws 'Map is updating, cannot calculate path!'. The actor is already spawned by then, so a throw here must be a WARNING - `selectionReset` in the output - not a FAILED verdict over completed work.
PROOF, not a non-error return. InPlay is the completion predicate (ActorComponent.cs:114); ActorSpawner.cs:23 defers DoEnterPlay when the level is not playing, so this is a wait rather than a read.

finally.//: Only the intermediates: the actor handle is the deliverable and the def handles are cheap to re-resolve. A plan that failed at step 2 never created most of these, and that is fine - a step inside `finally` never aborts the block.
The preload intermediates only. The ASSETS stay held - the loader owns them and the level releases them on teardown.
